title: Drupal core installer flaw exploited in the wild: anonymous site reinstall leads to takeover/RCE (SA-CORE-2026-017)
why: Drupal's security team published SA-CORE-2026-017 (Critical 18/25, CVE-2026-132165) on Nov 18 and warned that exploits may appear within hours or days; BleepingComputer, The Hacker News and The DropTimes covered it Nov 19. No attacks reported yet, and it is not in CISA KEV. Microsoft has nothing on it. Nov 19-20: Drupal's risk vector marks the exploit as E:Proof (proof of concept exists), and Horizon3 published an analysis; THN and Cyber Kendra covered it. Fixed in 10.6.22, 11.3.22 and 11.4.13. No in-the-wild reports yet; not in KEV. Nov 21: Horizon3, BleepingComputer and The Hacker News coverage shows a public proof of concept but no reported exploitation. Rechecked Nov 22 09Z: the collector saw no new CISA KEV entries since the Nov 20 batch, so still not in KEV. Nov 23 09Z: Drupal's advisory (modified Nov 21 16:14 UTC) now says the Security Team received a report that this was exploited on live sites as early as Nov 19 19:00 UTC. Vendor-confirmed exploitation, but still not in CISA KEV (the collector saw no new KEV entries), and Microsoft has nothing on it. Nov 24 09Z recheck: still not in CISA KEV (the only KEV additions on Nov 23 were MONAI Label and N-able MailAssure) and no Microsoft advisory.
action: Upgrade to Drupal 10.6.22, 11.3.22 or 11.4.13, and block web access to /core/install.php and make settings.php read-only for the web server.

title: Oracle Database: pre-auth RCE chain (Oracle Text CVE-2026-114819 + ORDS GraphQL CVE-2026-91609) with public PoC from Depthfirst
why: Depthfirst researcher Zheng Yu published proof-of-concept exploits on Nov 18, and The Hacker News reported them on Nov 19. One is a chain that reaches Oracle Database engine code and runs commands with no login, through an exposed ORDS GraphQL endpoint. Oracle patched the parts in its Nov 17 CSPU (CVE-2026-114819, CVSS 9.9) and Oct 20 CPU (CVE-2026-91609), but rates neither as exploitable without a login. No attacks have been seen. Neither CVE is in CISA KEV, and there is nothing from Microsoft. Rechecked Nov 19 17Z: no CISA KEV additions since the Nov 18 batch (Senserva KEV tracker), so still not in KEV. Rechecked Nov 20 09Z: no CISA KEV additions since the Nov 18 batch, so still not in KEV.
action: Apply Oracle's Oct 2026 CPU (ORDS) and Nov 17 CSPU (Oracle Text) now, and take ORDS/GraphQL endpoints off the internet until both are in place.
product: Oracle Database (Oracle Text) 19.3-19.32, 21.3-21.24, 23.4.0-23.26.3 with Oracle REST Data Services 24.2.0-26.2.1 exposed

title: GL.iNet GoodCloud cloud-management flaw exploited to plant malware on GL.iNet routers and KVM devices
why: GL.iNet's security notice (issued Nov 20, updated Nov 23) confirms an unauthorized party exploited a vulnerability in its GoodCloud remote-management service to install malware on some routers and KVM devices. BleepingComputer, The Hacker News, SecurityWeek and Cybernews covered it Nov 22-23; Cybernews cites researchers who found malware or older backdoors on 166 of 199 routers they analyzed. There is no CVE, it is not in CISA KEV, and there is no Microsoft signal. KVMs give the attacker a path to the connected computers. Nov 24 09Z recheck: still not in CISA KEV (the only KEV additions on Nov 23 were MONAI Label and N-able MailAssure) and no Microsoft advisory.
action: Install the GL.iNet security firmware for each router or KVM model, check devices for the infection indicator in GL.iNet's notice, and, if a KVM was infected, check the computers connected to it.
product: GL.iNet routers and remote KVMs managed through GoodCloud (security firmware per model, e.g. GL-MT3000/MT6000 4.11.1, KVM RM1 1.10.3)

affected.product: GL.iNet GL-AX1800 / AXT1800 / SFT1200 / X3000 / XE3000 firmware
GL.iNet KVM RM1 / RM1V2 / RM10 / RM10RC / RM1PE / RM4PE firmware

title: ConnectWise ScreenConnect CVE-2026-84869 exploited to run guest-pushed payloads on MSP technician PCs
why: Not ahead: CVE-2026-84869 has been in CISA KEV since Sep 11. New this run: The Hacker News (Nov 23) and Huntress report a campaign against MSP ScreenConnect servers that runs guest-pushed batch files on technician hosts and installs rogue ScreenConnect clients.
action: Update ScreenConnect servers and every technician client to the fixed release, and hunt for rogue ScreenConnect clients pointing at unknown relays.
product: ScreenConnect client (unpatched host/technician clients)

title: Xen Orchestra empty-object login token auth bypass (exploited) now tracked as CVE-2026-133469
why: The Xen Orchestra authentication bypass we have tracked since Nov 10 as exploited in the wild (vendor advisory VSA-2026-062, fixed 6.9.2/6.10.1) received CVE-2026-133469 on Nov 23 (NVD 9.8, GitHub advisory GHSA-2r3w-c2vx-fv5g). VulDB and CVEReports describe it as actively exploited. It is not in CISA KEV and there is no Microsoft signal. A Sploitus-listed "PoC" repo is from a publisher previously seen posting simulated labs, so it is not counted as public exploit code.
action: Upgrade Xen Orchestra to 6.9.2 or 6.10.1, revoke all existing authentication tokens, and review XO audit logs for unexpected REST logins.
product: Xen Orchestra (xo-server) before 6.9.2 / 6.10.1

title: FastUnlock: Windows 11 Narrator lock-screen bypass 0-day defeats BitLocker on fully patched 26H2 (public PoC)
why: On Nov 19 the researcher behind the MSNightmare account published FastUnlock on GitHub, a Windows Narrator lock-screen bypass he says gives code execution as the lock-screen account 'WsiAccount' and bypasses BitLocker on Windows 11 26H2 with the November patch. He suggests chaining it with SignDrop to elevate privileges. It spread via X, Hacker News and GitHub trending. There is no CVE, no MSRC advisory and no Microsoft statement yet. Not independently confirmed. Nov 20: The Hacker News, Cyber Press and Cryptika covered it; Cryptika says no Microsoft fix was identified as of Nov 20, and the November BitLocker fixes (CVE-2026-97015, CVE-2026-119832) are unrelated. Still no CVE or MSRC advisory. Nov 21-22: Cybernews, CyberSecurityNews and IT-Connect say it is still unpatched and Microsoft has not commented; still no CVE or MSRC advisory. Nov 22: WindowsForum reports that a security company reproduced the bypass. It needs physical access and does not break BitLocker encryption itself. Still no CVE, no MSRC advisory and no Microsoft fix (Aviatrix, Nov 21). Nov 23 17Z: still no CVE, MSRC advisory or fix (Cyber Kendra, Aviatrix, TechSpot). Nov 24 09Z recheck: still not in CISA KEV (the only KEV additions on Nov 23 were MONAI Label and N-able MailAssure) and no Microsoft advisory.
action: For high-risk laptops, require a BitLocker pre-boot PIN (TPM+PIN) and watch MSRC for a fix. If your accessibility policy allows it, consider blocking Narrator at the lock screen.
product: Windows 11 26H2 with the November 2026 update (researcher's claim)

title: Azure API Management Classic tiers flaw exploited to steal secrets (Equinor, Skagerak Energi); Microsoft mitigated Nov 19
why: Not ahead: Microsoft found the flaw Nov 18, mitigated it service-side Nov 19 and sent customers a critical advisory (non-public, per The Register). There is no public MSRC CVE. Norway's NSM (guidance Nov 20, updated Nov 23) says an unknown actor targeted APIM access tokens, secrets and named values at Equinor, Skagerak Energi and others.
action: If you run APIM Classic, rotate every named value, client secret, subscription key and management token stored in it, move secrets to Key Vault references, and review APIM activity logs from before Nov 19.
product: Azure API Management Classic tiers (v2 tiers not affected)

title: Danfoss refrigeration controllers: CVEs assigned for default-credential access (AK-SC 355/AK-SM 800, used in the supermarket sabotage wave) and an unauthenticated CGI overflow (AK-SM 8xxA)
why: Danfoss advisory DSA-2026-12-01 (published Nov 20) assigns CVE-2026-127057 (CVSS 9.9) to the factory default credentials on legacy AK-SC 355/AK-SM 800 controllers and CVE-2026-129713 (CVSS 9.3) to an unauthenticated stack overflow in AK-SM 8xxA. Reporting on the European refrigeration-sabotage wave (decryptiondigest, SOCRadar) names default credentials on internet-exposed AK-SM 800A/8xxA as an entry point. Neither new CVE is in CISA KEV. Whether 129713 is one of the six unpatched AK-SM800A flaws disclosed Nov 11 is not confirmed. Nov 24 09Z recheck: still not in CISA KEV (the only KEV additions on Nov 23 were MONAI Label and N-able MailAssure) and no Microsoft advisory.
action: Take AK-SC/AK-SM controllers off the internet (VPN only), change the default Supervisor credentials now, and follow DSA-2026-12-01 for AK-SM 8xxA firmware.
product: Danfoss legacy AK-SC 355 and AK-SM 800 Series (all versions); AK-SM 8xxA Series

title: MONAI Label path traversal zero-day added to CISA KEV (CVE-2026-133968)
why: CISA added CVE-2026-133968 to KEV on Nov 23 (THN Nov 24), so Microsoft-side tracking now exists; no longer ahead.
action: Find any MONAI Label servers, take them off untrusted networks, set MONAI_LABEL_AUTH_ENABLE=True and update to a build that includes the PR #1915 fix; hunt for unexpected files written outside the datastore.
product: MONAI Label (monailabel) 0.8.5 and earlier (fixed 0.8.6)

title: Idunno.AntiCsrf (legacy ASP.NET WebForms library) unauthenticated deserialization RCE exploited in the wild, no patch
why: Mandiant's disclosure MNDT-2026-0048 (last week) says active exploitation in the wild has been observed: one HTTP POST with any CSRF cookie value and a Base64 ObjectStateFormatter gadget chain runs code in w3wp.exe, no login needed. The Hacker News, SecurityOnline and CyberSecurityNews reported it Nov 23. It is not in CISA KEV (the collector saw no new KEV entries). It is a third-party library, so there will be no MSRC advisory, and there is no Microsoft Defender signal. No patch exists. Nov 24 09Z recheck: still not in CISA KEV (the only KEV additions on Nov 23 were MONAI Label and N-able MailAssure) and no Microsoft advisory.
action: Search Web.config files and bin/ folders for Idunno.AntiCsrf or AntiCsrfModule and remove it (replace with AntiForgery or ViewStateUserKey). If it was exposed, review IIS logs for anomalous .aspx POSTs and rotate machineKey and other Web.config secrets.
product: Idunno.AntiCsrf 0.9.1.0 and 0.9.1 Beta (all releases, no fix)

title: MoldyRoost malvertising delivers Coruna/DarkSword iOS exploit chains to steal crypto seed phrases
why: Confiant reports a May-Nov 2026 malvertising operation (480+ ad domains, 47 countries) serving Coruna, DarkSword, SilkPath and GhostWave iOS exploit kits. The named CVE-2023-43000 has been in CISA KEV since Mar 5, 2026 and Apple has patched the known chains, so not ahead.
action: Enforce current iOS versions via MDM and block devices below the latest release from corporate resources.
product: iOS (unpatched; known kits target up to iOS 18)

title: PostgreSQL CVE-2026-116331: low-privilege login role to OS code execution via type confusion (public Depthfirst PoC)
why: Depthfirst published a working exploit on Nov 18 (reported by The Hacker News, Nov 19). In it, a plain login role that uses only its default TEMPORARY privilege runs code as the database OS user. PostgreSQL fixed it on Nov 12. No exploitation in the wild has been reported, it is not in CISA KEV, and Microsoft has published no guidance (Azure Database for PostgreSQL status unknown). Rechecked Nov 19 17Z: no CISA KEV additions since the Nov 18 batch (Senserva KEV tracker), so still not in KEV. Rechecked Nov 20 09Z: no CISA KEV additions since the Nov 18 batch, so still not in KEV.
action: Upgrade PostgreSQL to 18.7/17.12/16.16/15.20/14.25, and revoke TEMPORARY from roles that do not need it.

title: ClickHouse integer-overflow write in binary row format reached by low-privilege user (public Depthfirst PoC, no CVE, no confirmed fix)
why: Depthfirst reproduced a shell on ClickHouse 26.7.5.10 from a user who only sets format_binary_max_string_size=0. The PoC was published Nov 18 (The Hacker News, Nov 19). It has no CVE and no confirmed fixed version, so it cannot be in CISA KEV, and Microsoft has published nothing. Rechecked Nov 19 17Z: no CISA KEV additions since the Nov 18 batch (Senserva KEV tracker), so still not in KEV. Rechecked Nov 20 09Z: no CISA KEV additions since the Nov 18 batch, so still not in KEV.
action: Restrict who can change settings on ClickHouse (use a readonly or settings-constraint profile that locks format_binary_max_string_size), and ask ClickHouse for a fixed build.
product: ClickHouse (26.7.5.10 tested)

title: N-able MailAssure (SpamExperts) SSRF CVE-2026-134624 added to CISA KEV
why: CISA added CVE-2026-134624 (the flaw behind the Mail Assure/SpamExperts breach tracked since Nov 19) to KEV on Nov 23; no longer ahead.
action: If you or your MSP use Mail Assure/SpamExperts, confirm you received N-able's guidance, then review quarantine-release and outbound-relay activity and rotate the portal and API credentials once access is restored.
product: Mail Assure and SpamExperts Hosted Cloud

title: Malicious npm package @leadstack/crm-connect installs Hermes Agent as a Telegram-controlled backdoor on servers
why: SafeDep (Nov 19, trending on Hacker News Nov 21) documents the package posing as a LeadStack CRM client that, on install, sets up the open-source Hermes Agent as a systemd service steered from the attacker's Telegram bot. No CVE, so it cannot be in CISA KEV; no Microsoft blog or Defender write-up seen. Nov 24 09Z recheck: still not in CISA KEV (the only KEV additions on Nov 23 were MONAI Label and N-able MailAssure) and no Microsoft advisory.
action: Search lockfiles, npm caches and CI logs for @leadstack/crm-connect; on any hit, isolate the host, remove the disguised systemd service and rotate credentials it could reach.
product: @leadstack/crm-connect (all published versions)

title: MySQL Server/Cluster optimizer flaw CVE-2026-101786: temp-table-only account to RCE (public Depthfirst PoC)
why: Depthfirst published a PoC on Nov 18 showing code execution on MySQL 26.7.0 from an account that can only create temporary tables. Oracle's Oct 20 advisory rates the flaw as needing high privileges. No exploitation has been seen, it is not in CISA KEV, and there is nothing from Microsoft. Rechecked Nov 19 17Z: no CISA KEV additions since the Nov 18 batch (Senserva KEV tracker), so still not in KEV. Rechecked Nov 20 09Z: no CISA KEV additions since the Nov 18 batch, so still not in KEV.
action: Update MySQL 26.7.x to the October 2026 fixed release, and remove CREATE TEMPORARY TABLES from accounts that do not need it.
product: MySQL Server and Cluster 26.7.0 to 26.7.1

title: Ruby2Shell (CVE-2026-132825): one-byte heap overflow in Ruby case conversion, pre-auth RCE on stock Rails and classic Sinatra
why: Ruby2Shell (GHSA-34m4-m9fh-gqp5) now has CVE-2026-132825 (Aikido, Astra; MITRE CVSS 7.4). Ruby maintainers know of private PoCs that achieve RCE in some scenarios, and Veria Labs plans a public PoC about a week after the Nov 19 disclosure. A Hacker News post says GitLab 19.6.0 still ships an affected Ruby. No exploitation reported, not in CISA KEV, and nothing from Microsoft. Nov 19: MITRE assigned CVE-2026-132825 (oss-security). Rechecked Nov 20 09Z: no CISA KEV additions since the Nov 18 batch, so still not in KEV. Nov 20: GnuPG says GitLab had to ship its Ruby2Shell update early; still not in KEV after the Nov 20 additions. Nov 24 09Z recheck: still not in CISA KEV (the only KEV additions on Nov 23 were MONAI Label and N-able MailAssure) and no Microsoft advisory.
action: Upgrade Ruby to 3.3.14, 3.4.13 or 4.0.10 and restart app processes. Check the Ruby bundled inside GitLab and other appliances or containers, and patch internet-facing Rails apps before the public PoC lands.
product: CRuby 2.4.0 through 3.3.13, 3.4.0-3.4.12, 4.0.0-4.0.9 (also bundled runtimes in GitLab and other self-hosted apps)

title: F5 BIG-IP out-of-band hotfixes: five critical unauthenticated TMM stack overflows (APM, iRules) that may allow RCE
why: F5's Nov 18 out-of-band notification (K000164058/K000164239) fixes critical stack overflows that let a remote unauthenticated attacker crash TMM and may allow code execution; BleepingComputer, THN and SecurityWeek cover it. No exploitation reported, not in CISA KEV, nothing from Microsoft. Shadowserver sees 177,000+ exposed BIG-IP and 14,600 APM instances. Nov 24 09Z recheck: still not in CISA KEV (the only KEV additions on Nov 23 were MONAI Label and N-able MailAssure) and no Microsoft advisory.
action: Check BIG-IP APM and iRule (including DNS::scrape) usage against F5's K articles and install the out-of-band hotfixes on exposed systems.
product: F5 BIG-IP (APM, iRules configurations, BIG-IP DNS DNS::scrape iRule)

title: Upload2Shell: Ghostscript Type 1 font-loader use-after-free escapes -dSAFER for command execution via uploads, mail and print pipelines
why: pwn.ai published Upload2Shell (CVE-2026-125396) this week. It is a use-after-free in Ghostscript's Type 1 font loader that crosses the -dSAFER sandbox and runs attacker-chosen commands as the rendering process. pwn.ai lists confirmed command execution in production or lab paths, including Google's document renderer (since fixed), WordPress Core uploads (separate CVE-2026-65640, fixed Aug 12) and unauthenticated IPP print jobs to Debian 13 CUPS. Artifex fixed it in Ghostscript 10.08.0 (Sep 8). oss-security, The Hacker News and CyberSecurityNews cover it. pwn.ai says per-product PoCs are not yet published, and no exploitation in the wild has been reported. It is not in CISA KEV, and there is no Microsoft advisory or Defender guidance. Nov 24 09Z recheck: still not in CISA KEV (the only KEV additions on Nov 23 were MONAI Label and N-able MailAssure) and no Microsoft advisory.
action: Update Ghostscript to 10.08.0 or your distro's package that fixes CVE-2026-125396, and check that upload, preview and print services do not pass untrusted files to Ghostscript (for example, disable PS/PDF/EPS coders in ImageMagick policy.xml).
product: Ghostscript before 10.08.0 (distro backports vary, e.g. Debian 13 fixed in 10.05.1~dfsg-1+deb13u2); reached through ImageMagick, WordPress Core uploads, CUPS and other renderers

title: PHP Nov 19 security release fixes 18 CVEs incl. critical RCEs (FPM request smuggling CVE-2026-129289, PHPAfterShell, session serializer)
why: PHP shipped 8.5.13/8.4.28/8.3.37/8.2.36 on Nov 19, fixing 18 CVEs (Aikido, BleepingComputer, The Hacker News, Infosecurity). The worst is CVE-2026-129289 (9.2): unauthenticated PHP-FPM request smuggling to code execution when the web server reuses backend connections. Several other session and use-after-free bugs are rated 9.2 RCE, including Depthfirst's 'PHPAfterShell' CVE-2026-126714. PHP says the critical issues need non-default or uncommon setups. No exploitation or public PoC is reported, none is in KEV, and Microsoft has nothing on them. Rechecked Nov 20 09Z: no CISA KEV additions since the Nov 18 batch, so still not in KEV.
action: Upgrade to PHP 8.5.13, 8.4.28, 8.3.37 or 8.2.36. Until then, disable persistent web-server-to-FPM connections and set session.upload_progress.enabled=0, and never expose FPM/LSAPI listeners to untrusted networks.
product: PHP 8.2 before 8.2.36, 8.3 before 8.3.37, 8.4 before 8.4.28, 8.5 before 8.5.13

title: Attackers used CyberPower PowerPanel Business UPS software as a SYSTEM execution channel on a domain controller to dump AD
why: In research published Nov 18, Symantec's Threat Intelligence team describes an intrusion where attackers uploaded .cmd scripts through PowerPanel Business's file-upload endpoint (TCP 3052) on a Windows domain controller. The PPB service (ppbed.exe) ran them as SYSTEM to copy the AD database and launch malware. Infosecurity Magazine also covered it. Symantec did not establish how the attackers got console access; earlier PPB advisories list hard-coded credentials and a default admin password. There is no new CVE and no KEV entry, and Microsoft has nothing on it. Rechecked Nov 20 09Z: no CISA KEV additions since the Nov 18 batch, so still not in KEV. Nov 24 09Z recheck: still not in CISA KEV (the only KEV additions on Nov 23 were MONAI Label and N-able MailAssure) and no Microsoft advisory.
action: Find PowerPanel Business installs, block TCP 3052 from non-admin networks, change default and admin credentials, and review the event-script folder for .cmd files you did not create.
product: PowerPanel Business (web console on TCP 3052)

title: Oracle E-Business Suite: CVE-2026-114924 auth bypass + CVE-2026-114925 REST RCE chain to unauthenticated OS command execution (12.2.3-12.2.15)
why: Horizon3 reverse engineered Oracle's November CSPU patch and published on Nov 19 that CVE-2026-114924 (authorization bypass) chains with CVE-2026-114925 (unrestricted class instantiation in REST Services) to give unauthenticated OS command execution on the EBS application tier over HTTP. Oracle reports no exploitation and no public exploit code was seen, but EBS was mass-exploited after similar disclosures earlier this year. Not in CISA KEV as of Nov 20 and no Microsoft signal. Nov 24 09Z recheck: still not in CISA KEV (the only KEV additions on Nov 23 were MONAI Label and N-able MailAssure) and no Microsoft advisory.
action: Apply the November 2026 Oracle CSPU EBS patches now; until then restrict access to EBS HTTP and REST endpoints to trusted networks.
product: Oracle E-Business Suite 12.2.3-12.2.15 (Application Object Library Core; Applications Framework REST Services)

title: phpAfterShell (CVE-2026-126714): PHP default file session handler can be made to deserialize attacker objects, leading to RCE with a gadget chain
why: depthfirst disclosed phpAfterShell on Nov 19 with an end-to-end demonstration: interrupting a write to PHP's default file-based session storage can splice sessions so session_start() returns attacker-chosen objects, which an app gadget chain can turn into code execution (CVSS 4.0 9.2). PHP fixed it in the Nov 19 releases; The Hacker News, Cycode and Ostorlab covered it. No exploitation reported, not in CISA KEV (only the October PHP2Shell CVEs are), and no Microsoft signal. Nov 24 09Z recheck: still not in CISA KEV (the only KEV additions on Nov 23 were MONAI Label and N-able MailAssure) and no Microsoft advisory.
action: Upgrade PHP to 8.5.13, 8.4.28, 8.3.37 or 8.2.36 (or 8.6.0); replace EOL 8.1-and-older runtimes.
product: PHP 8.2 before 8.2.36, 8.3 before 8.3.37, 8.4 before 8.4.28, 8.5 before 8.5.13; 8.1 and older (EOL) also affected

title: @fastify/express and @fastify/middie path-scoped middleware bypass: unauthenticated requests skip auth/rate-limit middleware (five CVEs, CVSS 9.1)
why: Fastify published GHSA-w877-hjcp-88rc and NVD added five CVSS 9.1 CVEs on Nov 21. URL decoding and normalisation mismatches between Fastify's router and the Express or middie middleware layer let an unauthenticated request reach a route handler while skipping the path-scoped authentication, authorization or rate-limit middleware meant to protect it. @fastify/express 4.0.10 fixes it. No public PoC or exploitation has been reported. It is not in CISA KEV, and there is no Microsoft guidance. Nov 24 09Z recheck: still not in CISA KEV (the only KEV additions on Nov 23 were MONAI Label and N-able MailAssure) and no Microsoft advisory.
action: Upgrade @fastify/express to 4.0.10 and @fastify/middie past 9.3.7, and move auth checks into Fastify hooks (onRequest/preHandler) instead of path-scoped middleware.
product: @fastify/express before 4.0.10; @fastify/middie 9.3.7 and earlier

title: better-auth phone-number plugin lets attackers claim unverified numbers and take over accounts via phone OTP sign-in
why: VulnCheck assigned CVE-2026-134322 on Nov 21 for a better-auth advisory (GHSA-q747-mqgr-4gh7) fixed in the Nov 3 security release. Sign-up and other flows save phone numbers before they are verified, and phone-OTP sign-in then uses that number to pick the account, so an attacker can attach a victim's number and take over the account (CVSS 4.0 8.6, needs some user interaction). No PoC or exploitation has been reported. It is not in CISA KEV, and there is no Microsoft guidance. Nov 24 09Z recheck: still not in CISA KEV (the only KEV additions on Nov 23 were MONAI Label and N-able MailAssure) and no Microsoft advisory.
action: If you use better-auth with the phone number plugin, upgrade to 1.7.16 (or 1.8.0-beta.5) and review accounts whose phone numbers were never verified.
product: better-auth 0.4.12-beta.7 before 1.7.16 and 1.8.0-beta.0 before 1.8.0-beta.5 (phone number plugin)

title: Rclone serve sftp --auth-proxy authentication bypass via cache key that omits credentials
why: NVD published CVE-2026-134352 (CVSS 9.2) on Nov 21. In rclone serve sftp with --auth-proxy, the cache key does not include the authentication material, so a later login can reuse an earlier authenticated session. It only affects that configuration. Fixed in 1.76.0. The only source is the NVD record, with no PoC or exploitation reported. It is not in CISA KEV, and there is no Microsoft guidance. Nov 24 09Z recheck: still not in CISA KEV (the only KEV additions on Nov 23 were MONAI Label and N-able MailAssure) and no Microsoft advisory.
action: Upgrade rclone to 1.76.0 wherever 'rclone serve sftp --auth-proxy' runs, or stop that service until you can.
product: Rclone 1.51.0 before 1.76.0 (serve sftp with --auth-proxy)

title: Synology DSM / BeeStation OS OAuth API argument injection: unauthenticated arbitrary file read/write (CVSS 9.8, Synology-SA-26:21)
why: Synology published Synology-SA-26:21 around Nov 19 for CVE-2026-120382 (CVSS 9.8, no authentication or user interaction needed). NVD published it Nov 22, and SOC Prime and DEV Community covered it Nov 21; as of Nov 20 some branches were still marked 'Ongoing' in the advisory. No exploitation or public PoC reported (OffSeq: not known to be exploited, Nov 23). Not in CISA KEV; Microsoft has no signal on it. Nov 24 09Z recheck: still not in CISA KEV (the only KEV additions on Nov 23 were MONAI Label and N-able MailAssure) and no Microsoft advisory.
action: Update DSM to the fixed build for your branch; where no build is out yet, deactivate the OAuth Service package and keep DSM off the internet.
product: DiskStation Manager (DSM) 6.2-7.4 before the fixed builds; BeeStation OS 1.5

title: Spring Data Elasticsearch SpEL injection through @Query method arguments (RCE when untrusted input reaches a repository query)
why: Spring published CVE-2026-123886 (High, CVSS 8.8) on Nov 19, and NVD on Nov 23. Untrusted method arguments are evaluated as SpEL inside string-based @Query methods, which can lead to code execution. Fixed in 6.0.9 and 6.1.3. There is no public PoC or exploitation, it is not in CISA KEV, and there is no Microsoft signal. Nov 24 09Z recheck: still not in CISA KEV (the only KEV additions on Nov 23 were MONAI Label and N-able MailAssure) and no Microsoft advisory.
action: Upgrade Spring Data Elasticsearch to 6.1.3 or 6.0.9 (the 5.x line is listed as affected through 5.5.13 with no open-source fix named) and find string-based @Query methods that take user input.

title: AutoGPT Platform ships a public default JWT secret: forge admin tokens (CVE-2026-130169, CVSS 10)
why: Disclosed Nov 23 (NVD/CVE, CVSS 10): AutoGPT Platform deployments that keep the hardcoded HS256 key from .env.default accept forged JWTs for any user or admin. VulDB lists AutoGPT 0.8.0 as the upgrade. No exploitation report found; OffSeq lists honeypot/exposure data without detail. Not in CISA KEV, no Microsoft signal.
action: Rotate the JWT secret in every self-hosted AutoGPT deployment (never use the .env.default value), upgrade past 0.7.4, and invalidate existing sessions.
product: AutoGPT Platform 0.6.26 through 0.7.4

title: Chrome critical sandbox escape in Variations (CVE-2026-134401) fixed in 158.0.8127.88; Edge fix not yet seen
why: Google shipped Chrome 158.0.8127.88/.89 on Nov 23 for a Critical-rated Variations flaw that lets a crafted HTML page run code outside the sandbox (NVD 9.6). No exploitation reported. Not in CISA KEV, and no Microsoft Edge security release or MSRC entry for this CVE was found as of Nov 24 09Z (the latest Edge security note found covers CVE-2026-125350).
action: Force Chrome to 158.0.8127.88+ across the fleet (relaunch required) and watch for the matching Microsoft Edge security update.
product: Google Chrome before 158.0.8127.88 (and Chromium-based browsers)

title: OpenSSL EVP_EncodeBlock() integer overflow leads to heap buffer overflow (CVE-2026-121481, CVSS 9.8)
why: OpenSSL published CVE-2026-121481 on Nov 18: calling EVP_EncodeBlock() with an input length near INT_MAX overflows the output-size calculation and writes past the caller's buffer. The fix PR (openssl #33652) says the formal advisory is still pending; it reached Hacker News on Nov 20. Exploitation needs an application that base64-encodes ~2 GB of attacker-influenced data; no exploit or attacks reported, not in CISA KEV, no Microsoft signal. Nov 24 09Z recheck: still not in CISA KEV (the only KEV additions on Nov 23 were MONAI Label and N-able MailAssure) and no Microsoft advisory.
action: Inventory OpenSSL 4.x builds and update to 4.0.4 or 4.1.1; watch for the pending OpenSSL advisory to confirm whether 3.x branches are affected.
product: OpenSSL 4.0 before 4.0.4 and 4.1 before 4.1.1 (3.x status unclear in sources)

title: WhatsApp for Android ad-reply URL validation flaw (IP leak) suspected exploited in scam campaigns
why: WhatsApp says it found the bug while disrupting a scam campaign and suspects it was used to make scam messages look credible (The Hacker News, SecurityWeek, Security Affairs, Nov 20). Not in CISA KEV; nothing from Microsoft (not a Microsoft product). Nov 24 09Z recheck: still not in CISA KEV (the only KEV additions on Nov 23 were MONAI Label and N-able MailAssure) and no Microsoft advisory.
action: Push WhatsApp / WhatsApp Business for Android 2.26.17.4 or later on managed Android devices.
product: WhatsApp and WhatsApp Business for Android before 2.26.17.4

title: simple-git argument injection: --exec bypasses allowUnsafePack guard for command execution (fixed 4.1.0)
why: NVD and a VulnCheck advisory published CVE-2026-134815 on Nov 22 (CVSS 4.0 9.2). The --exec option to ls-remote, archive, fetch-pack or send-pack bypasses simple-git's allowUnsafePack guard. No exploitation or public PoC reported (OffSeq: not known to be exploited). Not in CISA KEV; nothing from Microsoft. Nov 24 09Z recheck: still not in CISA KEV (the only KEV additions on Nov 23 were MONAI Label and N-able MailAssure) and no Microsoft advisory.
action: Upgrade simple-git to 4.1.0 or later (check transitive dependencies with npm ls simple-git), and never pass user-controlled strings as git options.
product: simple-git (npm) before 4.1.0

title: GPGME double free via crafted long OpenPGP user ID (affects Gpg4win, mail clients, Samba, Flatpak)
why: GnuPG advisory (Nov 20, forwarded to oss-security) rates it critical: a crafted key can trigger a double free usable to exfiltrate data, RCE not ruled out; disclosed early because of the Ruby2Shell GitLab update. No exploitation or public PoC seen; not in CISA KEV; no Microsoft guidance. Nov 21: oss-security thread notes Red Hat had patched this downstream years ago; still no PoC or exploitation. Nov 24 09Z recheck: still not in CISA KEV (the only KEV additions on Nov 23 were MONAI Label and N-able MailAssure) and no Microsoft advisory.
action: Update GPGME to 2.3.1 (Gpg4win 5.1.2 on Windows) and rebuild statically linked tools; apply distro updates as they land.
product: GPGME before 2.3.1 (Gpg4win before 5.1.2)
